 1                RABBI LOEVINGER:   Last week -- 

 2   yeah, somebody got it.

 3                Last week in our biblical reading 

 4   we read a story in the Book of Numbers of a man 

 5   named Korach, who challenged Moses for the 

 6   leadership of the Israelites.  And Korach sought 

 7   a position of leadership not out of a desire to 

 8   serve, but out of a desire to rule for his own 

 9   sense of power and wanting glory and dominion 

10   over others.

11                And this kind of leadership causes 

12   division, strife and, in the story we read in 

13   the Book of Numbers, even death.

14                There is a resolution at the end of 

15   the story when Moses affirms to his brother 

16   Aaron, the high priest of the Israelites, that 

17   leadership does not mean only power and glory 

18   for the leader, but rather leadership means 

19   service, bearing in mind the entire people and 

20   their needs, bearing in mind that you serve a 

21   greater community and a greater good -- a kind 

22   of leadership that is now called servant 

23   leadership, which is, in its root, biblical 

24   leadership.  

25                And this is the kind of leadership 


                                                                3966

 1   that I pray to the source of my strength that 

 2   all of us in this chamber are blessed to 

 3   accomplish.  This is true leadership:  Service, 

 4   humility, bound together with others through the 

 5   values we all share.  Values like healing, hope, 

 6   justice, mercy, fairness, equality, dignity and 

 7   generosity.  

 8                We believe many things in this 

 9   wonderfully diverse State of New York.  We have 

10   many faiths, and some of us have no particular 

11   religious faith, but we are bound together in a 

12   commitment to serve.

13                And so I turn to the one I call 

14   God, the source of my strength, the source of my 

15   wisdom, who you may know through a different 

16   name or through a different experience.  But I 

17   hope you will turn to that source of meaning in 

18   your life and find that core of values that can 

19   bind you to others and the common work of 

20   leadership for our great state -- the values 

21   that bind us together as a citizenry, and the 

22   values that will bring our state and our common 

23   mission together into a great future together.

24                I thank God for the strength that 

25   we may all accomplish this, and I thank you for
